message.content: One of the most celebrated and widely recognized works of the 19th‑century sculpture canon is **Auguste Rodin’s “The Kiss” (1889)**. Created toward the end of the century, this bronze pair of lovers has become emblematic of Romanticism’s emotional intensity and Rodin’s mastery of form and texture. Its influence spread across Europe and America, inspiring countless reproductions, adaptations, and scholarly discussions, cementing its status as a cultural touchstone of the era.
